summary: colorstack ships remote MSI dropper and host-fingerprint exfiltration disguised as a color library
details: The package advertises itself as a color library but exports two APIs whose behavior is unrelated to color rendering. newcolors.colors() downloads opaque bytes from a hardcoded endpoint at https://www.fastsyncapi.com/v1/colors and executes them: on Windows it invokes msiexec.exe with /i /qn /norestart to silently install the downloaded MSI and then launches a hardcoded executable path (C:\Program Files\AppHostRegistrationVerifier\AppHostRegistrationVerifier.exe); on macOS/Linux it hands the downloaded file to open/xdg-open. newcolors.update() collects the machine hostname, locale-derived country code, and a SHA-256 fingerprint computed over the hostname concatenated with uuid.getnode() (MAC address) and POSTs them to https://www.fastsyncapi.com/v1/update, where the server issues activation tokens that gate subsequent binary downloads. The PyPI name (colorstack), import name (newcolors), README example (colorsv1('Sky Blue')), and __all__ exports frame these operations as color/version helpers; only colorsv1 actually manipulates colors. The colors() and update() functions constitute a remote-binary dropper and a device-inventory channel to a hardcoded third-party endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
